must_remember: In the j-j coupling scheme, the spin-orbit interaction energy for each electron is significantly larger than the electrostatic repulsion between electrons.
j-j coupling predominantly occurs in heavy multi-electron atoms with high atomic numbers ($Z$).
For each electron, the orbital angular momentum $l_i$ and spin angular momentum $s_i$ couple to form individual total angular momentum $j_i = l_i + s_i$.
In j-j coupling, neither total orbital angular momentum $L$ nor total spin angular momentum $S$ are good quantum numbers.
The resultant total angular momentum $J$ of the atom is obtained by the vector sum of individual $j_i$ vectors: $J = \sum j_i$.

glossary.meaning: An angular momentum coupling scheme where individual spin-orbit interactions are stronger than residual electrostatic interactions.
The vector sum of the orbital angular momentum $l_i$ and spin angular momentum $s_i$ of a single electron.
The vector sum of all individual electron total angular momenta $j_i$ in an atom.
The interaction between an electron's spin magnetic moment and the magnetic field created by its orbital motion around the nucleus.
